question: Can the NFRDI Baggao freshwater-sanctuary catch report provide safe, spatially precise, species-level fish records for Cagayan Valley?

sourcesReviewed.citation: Gibe, G. P., Mangabat, C. B., Ballad, E. L., Ame, E. C., Perez, M. R., & Ramos, M. T. (2023). Impacts of Freshwater Fish Sanctuaries on Fish and Crustacean Diversity, Catch, and Household Income of Fisherfolk in Baggao, Cagayan, Philippines. The Philippine Journal of Fisheries, 30(2), 199–211. https://doi.org/10.31398/tpjf/30.2.2022-0039
sourcesReviewed.access: Full 13-page official NFRDI repository PDF and item record reviewed.

reportedScope.catchDataPeriod: Table 3 reports barangay-level fish production for 2020 and 2021; Table 4 reports sanctuary-level fish/crustacean composition for January–December 2021. The interviews and key-informant interviews were conducted February–March 2022; these periods are distinct.
reportedScope.methodSummary: Structured interviews with 59 registered fisherfolk and key-informant interviews were conducted February–March 2022; photographs were used as fish-identification visual aids. The article also says secondary monthly fish-production and sanctuary-status data came from agencies and literature. It reports aggregate barangay production for 2020/2021 and sanctuary-by-taxon composition for calendar year 2021, but does not establish a specimen/voucher or capture-event crosswalk for those labels.

taxonomicAndEvidenceLimits.reportedResolution: Genus-level labels such as Anguilla sp., Oreochromis sp., Trichopodus sp., Crenimugil sp., Macrobrachium sp., Clarias sp., Arius sp., Glossogobius sp. and Gambusia sp.; the paper also includes freshwater crab and prawn groups. These are respondent/source labels, not species-level identifications.
sourceStringConflicts: Carp is printed as Ciprinus sp. in one table but Cyprinus sp. in another table and figure.
Mudfish is printed as Chana sp. in a table but Channa sp. in the figure.
Tilapia is printed as Oreochomis sp. in the figure but Oreochromis sp. elsewhere.
Crab and garfish genus spellings vary between Sundathelphusa/Suldathelphusa and Hyporhamphus/Hyphorhamphus.
taxonomicAndEvidenceLimits.catchInterpretation: The paper reports aggregate catches/composition for named sanctuary sites and separates recorded fishing in buffer zones from no-take/protected zones, but provides no specimen/voucher or individual capture-event crosswalk and no authoritative spatial boundary geometry. A historical aggregate label is not a species-level specimen occurrence, current distribution, safe-fishing advisory, or permission to fish within a protected area.

rights.pdfLicense: CC BY-NC 4.0, stated on the article PDF's final page.
rights.handling: The article is noncommercial-only. No table, map, photo, abundance value, or full-text passage was copied into the repository. No Bangwit app reuse is approved or inferred.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Department of Agriculture–Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Region 2. (2025-02-19). UK Ambassador, ZSL and BFAR Visit Conservation Site in Baggao, Cagayan.
sourcesReviewed.access: Official BFAR Region 2 public notice reviewed.
sourcesReviewed.reportedScope: The notice says three freshwater protected areas were established in Baggao and gives barangay/name associations for Bluewater Falls, Duba Cave and Hot Spring; it describes a broader project goal for a network along the Pared River Catchment.
sourcesReviewed.limits: The notice supplies no sanctuary polygon, technical boundary, ordinance copy, coordinates, species checklist, or current site-specific access rule. It is a management/status lead only.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Piper, A., Belen, A., Villanueva, B., & Gollock, M. (2022). Residence, activity patterns and behaviour of the giant mottled eel Anguilla marmorata in two freshwater protected areas in the Philippines. Aquatic Conservation: Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems, 32(10), 1606–1617. https://doi.org/10.1002/aqc.3870
sourcesReviewed.access: Wiley full-text article reviewed for species evidence, sampling dates, study site names and methods.

reportedScope.parentWatercourse: Near the headwaters of Pared River, a tributary of the Cagayan River
reportedScope.method: Capture and tagging with acoustic telemetry and passive integrated transponder tags, with tracking in the two protected-area reaches.
reportedScope.speciesFinding: The paper reports catches within the protected areas were almost exclusively Anguilla marmorata; only two Anguilla bicolor individuals were encountered.

taxonomicAndEvidenceLimits.interpretation: Historical, direct species-level evidence for the sampled protected-area reaches only. It is not a whole-river checklist, abundance estimate for today, or current catchability/safety status.
taxonomicAndEvidenceLimits.siteCrosswalk: The paper uses Hot Springs and Duba without naming barangays. The 2023–2027 BFAR FMA-1 management framework separately lists Hot Spring Fish Sanctuary in Asinga-via and Duba Cave Fish Sanctuary in San Miguel, Baggao, supporting the name and barangay crosswalk. The study's exact 1 km reaches and receiver array have not been matched to authoritative sanctuary boundaries.
taxonomicAndEvidenceLimits.coordinatesAndGeometry: The paper includes site-location information, but no coordinates or geometry were copied into Bangwit.

rights.license: The publisher page labels the article Open Access, but this review did not capture its item-specific reuse license. Verify the exact license before copying article content or admitting article-derived records.
rights.handling: Only concise bibliographic and evidence-limit metadata are summarized. No paper table, figure, coordinate, telemetry data or article text is copied into Bangwit.

crossSourceAssessment.nameCrosswalk: The 2023 article and 2025 BFAR notice name three Baggao sites, while the 2023–2027 BFAR FMA-1 management framework lists Hot Spring Fish Sanctuary in Asinga-via and Duba Cave Fish Sanctuary in San Miguel. Those official names and barangays align with the shortened Hot Springs and Duba names used by the telemetry paper; retain source spellings and distinguish administrative-name corroboration from exact reach boundaries.
crossSourceAssessment.spatialResolution: The 2023 survey gives named sites and barangays but no authoritative polygons. The 2022 telemetry paper samples two 1 km protected-area reaches near Pared River headwaters. BFAR's official list supports their name/barangay crosswalk, but no boundary dataset has been matched to the actual study reaches; do not draw a sanctuary polygon from names or receiver locations.
crossSourceAssessment.piper2022SpeciesEvidence: The telemetry study provides direct, historical species-level evidence of Anguilla marmorata and a small number of Anguilla bicolor in the sampled Hot Springs and Duba protected areas during 2018–2020. It does not establish current presence or a complete Pared River fish checklist.
crossSourceAssessment.habitatCoverage: Inland freshwater sanctuaries, waterfall/cave/spring settings and associated buffer zones. This is a named-site lead, not coverage of all Baggao waters or the Pared River Catchment.

disposition.reason: The 2023 article relies partly on interviews and secondary records with genus-level and internally inconsistent labels, distinct survey/catch periods, and no voucher or event-level crosswalk. The 2022 telemetry study adds historical species-level eel evidence and BFAR sources support the site names/barangays, but the exact study-reach boundaries and item-specific reuse license remain unverified. No public reuse permission is available.

nextAction: Continue the Region II inland-water sweep using independently accessible primary surveys and official waterbody inventories. For Baggao, obtain the 2016 barangay ordinance and authoritative technical sanctuary/buffer-zone boundaries to match the 2022 study's 1 km reaches; verify the article's item-specific reuse license and seek current site-resolved monitoring before public use. Do not show fishing permissions, no-take polygons, or public species rows until boundaries, current evidence and rights are independently reviewed.

sources.supports: Official NFRDI repository item record, authors, publication year, abstract, respondent survey summary, and repository file link.
Full 13-page article, methods, site descriptions, source taxon labels, buffer-zone catch distinction, internal name variants, and CC BY-NC 4.0 statement.
Official BFAR Region 2 notice about three Baggao freshwater protected areas and the Pared River Catchment project.

Peer-reviewed telemetry study of Hot Springs and Duba protected-area reaches near Pared River headwaters; reports historical Anguilla marmorata dominance and two Anguilla bicolor individuals. BFAR supports the name/barangay crosswalk, but no study-reach boundary polygon is available.

DA-BFAR FMA-1 Management Framework Table 14 lists Hot Spring Fish Sanctuary in Asinga-via and Duba Cave Fish Sanctuary in San Miguel, Baggao; it corroborates names and barangays but supplies no mapped boundaries for the telemetry study reaches.
